title: SEC-000003: Message-level integrity and freshness for safety-relevant CAN messages
statement: For every CAN identifier whose payload influences a safety function, the BMS master software shall verify, before the payload is passed to its receive callback, a rolling counter that establishes freshness, an integrity check that a bus peer cannot produce without the shared secret, and a data-length code matching the length expected for that identifier; a frame failing any of the three shall be rejected before the callback is invoked and shall raise a diagnosis entry.
rationale: Dispatch on identifier alone means that any node that can transmit on the bus can present a frame that the master accepts as genuine, because an identifier is not a credential. This is the highest-consequence exposure identified in the TARA, because the affected identifiers carry the cell voltage, cell temperature and pack current signals on which the safety requirements depend. All three checks are required and none is redundant: without the counter an authentic frame can be replayed indefinitely; without the integrity check the counter is forgeable by any bus peer; without the length check a short frame can be interpreted as if trailing bytes were meaningful (TARA threat THR-005, TARA mitigation MIT-004).

acceptance_criteria.measure: Frames with a valid identifier and no valid counter, integrity or length, accepted by the dispatch layer in a 24 h injection campaign
Previously recorded valid frames re-presented out of sequence and accepted
Frames whose data-length code differs from the configured length for that identifier and which reach the callback
Time from end of frame reception to the integrity verdict being available
Diagnosis entries raised per rejected frame, distinguishing counter, integrity and length failures

Genuine frames rejected under nominal bus conditions over a 24 h campaign whose observed genuine-frame population is at least 3 x 10^6 frames. Pass is 0 rejections observed over that population, which is a one-sided 95 percent upper confidence bound of 1 x 10^-6 on the rate by the rule of three (3/n <= 1e-6 for n >= 3e6). The integrity value used on this interface shall be at least 22 bits, which is the width for which a per-frame false rejection probability of 2^-w stays below the rate this criterion bounds over that population.

safety_allocation.mitigation: Security mitigation supporting the freedom-from-interference assumption of the cell-voltage and SOA requirements. asil is recorded as not_applicable because this is a security requirement and ISO 26262 does not allocate an ASIL to it; the trace to the FSR records the requirement whose assurance is at stake, not an ASIL allocation.

standards_mappings.reference: Clause 15.4 (mitigation concept); asset-integrity protection per Clause 8.5
standards_mappings.rationale: Named for traceability of intent only. No ISO/SAE 21434 work product exists, no conformance is claimed and no review has taken place.

standards_mappings.reference: Part 4, Clause 7 and Part 6, Clause 7 (protection of safety mechanisms from unintended effects)

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: First issue. Forward-engineered security requirement 'message-integrity-freshness-safety-bus' for the synthetic_reference project. Derived from threat analysis FB2-SAF-TAR-000001.

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: Replaced the absolute '0 genuine frames rejected over 24 h' acceptance criterion with a bounded rate, a stated population the bound is demonstrated over, and a minimum integrity value width that makes the bound achievable. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000028. The old criterion was unsatisfiable and non-discriminating at the same time: a keyed integrity value of width w rejects a genuine frame with probability 2^-w, so over a 24 h campaign the expected number of genuine rejections is n * 2^-w, non-zero for any practical w; meanwhile an implementation that rejected every frame would satisfy the criterion vacuously, and would also satisfy the other criteria in this record vacuously. The new criterion is 0 rejections observed over a genuine-frame population of at least 3 x 10^6 in a 24 h campaign, which by the rule of three (0 failures in n trials gives a one-sided 95 percent upper bound of 3/n) is a bound of 1 x 10^-6 on the rate; and it requires the integrity value on the interface to be at least 22 bits, which is the width for which 2^-w stays below that rate over that population. The three statements are mutually consistent, so the criterion is now achievable by a correct implementation of adequate width and is not satisfied by an always-rejecting one (~100 percent) or by a 16-bit one (~1.5e-5 per frame). The criterion is therefore STRICTER in discriminating power than the zero it replaces, and it is also a harder engineering obligation, because it constrains the width of the integrity value where the zero constrained nothing. The absolute zeros that remain in this record are the ones that are decidable by the check existing - injected frames accepted, replayed frames accepted, length-mismatch frames reaching the callback, control-byte transitions - and those are over countable events on a channel where no collision is involved, so they are unchanged and were deliberately not relaxed. The verification measure FB2-VER-TMS-000018 and its execution record were regenerated against the new criterion in the same revision set. No ASIL value, safety_goal_ref, statement clause or verification approach was changed.

real_source_presence: Control ABSENT at the dispatch layer. In the real foxBMS 2 source, src/app/driver/can/can.c:643-692 accepts a frame on hardware mailbox acceptance and on a data-lost indication (retval == CAN_HAL_RETVAL_NO_DATA_LOST at :657), which is a loss report and not a security check, then copies all eight data bytes at :675-682 without comparing the received data-length code against an expected length. src/app/driver/can/can.c:1015-1031 then matches a frame against the configured table on (canNode, id, idType) alone at :1021-1023 and invokes the registered callback at :1025. No rolling counter, integrity field or length check is applied at this layer. SCOPE LIMIT, stated explicitly: the per-message receive callbacks were NOT individually audited for this requirement, so this requirement asserts the absence only at the shared dispatch layer and does not assert that no individual callback performs its own check. A detective control IS present and is credited: CAN receive queue overflow raises DIAG_ID_CAN_RX_QUEUE_FULL (can.c:684-690, configured DIAG_WARNING / DIAG_SEN_EVENT_1 / DIAG_EVALUATION_ENABLED in src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.c:165), which is TARA mitigation MIT-007. Anchors FB2-SRC-COD-000065, FB2-SRC-COD-000066.
real_source_control_status_note: The control this requirement specifies is NOT present in the real foxBMS 2 source at commit 308028fb.
